original_intent.statement: Provide gated autonomous implementation from an approved code plan.

revisions.intent: Keep gated plan execution while assigning unit/component TDD to code-implementer and keeping QA for separate E2E work.
success_criteria: Blocker retry and review caps remain

revisions.intent: Keep explicitly invoked, approved code-plan execution while reducing mechanical prompt-audit constraints, resolving predictable user/auth/E2E dependencies during planning, selecting task-specific models and thinking within actual platform controls, and reporting task allocation and progress clearly.
success_criteria: Approval covers concrete scope and quality choices; routine execution does not reopen settled decisions.
Human authentication, E2E target/data authority, expected behavior, and downstream consent are resolved or explicitly staged before dependent execution.
Role/model/effort routing uses task complexity, visual needs, platform support and effective runtime evidence.
Task allocation, execution progress and final evidence use adaptable user-facing templates.
Structured checks preserve meaningful consistency and ownership without treating field counts or prose keywords as approval authority.
Unit/component work retains implementation ownership; QA stays independent E2E; existing retry/review-loop defaults remain bounded.
non_goals: Auto-triggering implement-plan or broadening its code-only workflow to non-code primary deliverables
Bypassing user/project/security permissions or downstream skill consent
Guaranteeing zero interaction despite expired access or new consequential facts
Changing shared agent definitions/platform mapping, live installation, publication, commit or push

approval.source: User request in current 2026-10-02 conversation: improve implement-plan for less prompt-audit rigidity, minimal interaction after approval, planning-time E2E/auth readiness, researched platform/model/thinking mapping, and task/progress output templates.
approval.reason: The current request explicitly authorizes these behavior changes; source-only maintenance retains implementation approval and external-action authority boundaries.
